extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners) on drafting and handling Office actions: addressing applicant arguments, documenting withdrawals or new grounds of rejection, treating each claim, prioritizing examination, and procedural requirements for signatures, mailing, and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of previous rejection and reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the withdrawal of the previous rejection results in the allowance of the claims, the reasons, which form the basis for the withdrawal of the previous rejection, may be included in a reasons for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.38.01 may be used. See MPEP §1302.14. If applicant’s arguments are persuasive and the examiner determines that the previous rejection should be withdrawn but that, upon further consideration, a new ground of rejection should be made, form paragraph 7.38.02 may be used. See MPEP §706.07(a) to determine whether the Office action may be made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of ground of rejection applied to new/amended claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection of record is to be applied to a new or amended claim, specific identification of that ground of rejection should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identification as by citation of the paragraph in the former Office letter in which the rejection was originally stated so the basis for the rejection applied to the new/amended claim is clear and traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering asserted advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant's reply asserts that prior art does not teach or inherently yield one or more advantages urged to warrant a patent, the examiner should state reasons on the record if the asserted advantages are insufficient to overcome the rejection(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reasons in the action following the assertion so applicant and the Patent Trial and Appeal Board know the advantages were considered. See MPEP §716 et seq. and 37 CFR 1.132. Case law (In re Herrmann; In re Soni) illustrates the importance of addressing such assertions—failure to rebut may force acceptance of applicant's assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37 — Arguments are not persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.37 where applicant’s arguments have been fully considered but are not persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must address all arguments which have not already been responded to in the statement of the rejection, and provide explanation in the bracket as to non-persuasiveness. Form paragraphs 7.37 through 7.37.13 may be used where applicant’s arguments are not persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38 — Arguments are moot because of new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.38 when applicant’s arguments have been considered but are moot because a new ground of rejection does not rely on any reference applied in the prior rejection for any teaching specifically challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must still address any arguments presented by the applicant which are still relevant to any references being applied. In bracket insert claim numbers, etc., as directed by the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38.01 — Arguments persuasive; previous rejection/objection withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant’s arguments have been fully considered and are persuasive, the prior rejection/objection may be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.38.01 should identify the applicant remarks (page/line numbers) forming the basis for withdrawal, identify the subject matter (claim, figure, specification, abstract, etc.), and insert the rejection or objection withdrawn. Follow bracket instructions in the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38.02 — Arguments persuasive; new ground(s) of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant’s arguments are persuasive as to the prior rejection but further consideration leads to a new ground of rejection, withdraw the prior rejection and make the new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.38.02 must identify applicant remarks (page/line), claim numbers, statutory basis for the previous rejection, and insert the new ground(s) of rejection (e.g., different interpretation, newly found prior art) with an explanation of the new rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Age of reference(s) (¶ 7.37.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions that reference patents are old are not persuasive absent a showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem notwithstanding knowledge of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Wright. This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37 and bracketed to restate applicant’s age-of-reference argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Bodily incorporation (¶ 7.37.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is not whether features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into a primary reference; rather, what the combined teachings would have suggested to one of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Keller. Briefly restate applicant’s argument in bracket 1. Use only after form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Hindsight reasoning (¶ 7.37.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: An obviousness judgment necessarily reconstructs based on hindsight, but it is proper so long as it only takes into account knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time and not knowledge gleaned only from the applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re McLaughlin. Use after form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: No teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine (¶ 7.37.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness may be established by combining or modifying teachings of prior art where there is some teaching, suggestion, or motivation to do so found in the references or in knowledge generally available to one skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Fine; In re Jones; KSR v. Teleflex. Explain where the teaching/suggestion/motivation is found (in references or general knowledge). Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Nonanalogous art (¶ 7.37.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must be either in the field of the inventor's endeavor or reasonably pertinent to the problem addressed to be relied upon as a basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Oetiker. Identify the reference alleged nonanalogous and explain why it is analogous. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Number of references (¶ 7.37.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a large number of references in a rejection does not, without more, weigh against the obviousness of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Gorman. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Result not contemplated by prior art (¶ 7.37.07)
rubrics_metrics.description: A result that flows naturally from following the suggestion of the prior art cannot be the basis for patentability when the differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Ex parte Obiaya. Briefly restate applicant's arguments about results not contemplated by prior art. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Arguing limitations not claimed (¶ 7.37.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot rely on features not recited in the rejected claim(s); limitations from the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Van Geuns. Recite the features relied upon by applicant that are not in the claims. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Intended use (¶ 7.37.09)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of intended use must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art to patentably distinguish; if prior art structure can perform the intended use, it meets the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claim(s) and restate the recitation. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Limitation(s) in preamble (¶ 7.37.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preamble language that does not provide distinct definition is not considered a limitation when the body of the claim describes a complete invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Pitney Bowes v. Hewlett-Packard and MPEP §2111.02. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: General allegation of patentability (¶ 7.37.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that amount to a general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) because they do not point out how the claim language patentably distinguishes from references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.37 as a precursor; explain non-compliance with 1.111(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Novelty not clearly pointed out (¶ 7.37.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that do not clearly point out the patentable novelty in view of the art fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c) and do not show how amendments avoid the references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the deficiency with respect to 1.111(c). Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Arguing against references individually (¶ 7.37.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where rejections are based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Keller; In re Merck. Briefly restate applicant's arguments. Precede with 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid piecemeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided; the examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, while avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply rejections on lack of disclosure, enablement, indefiniteness, res judicata where appropriate even if prior art rejection appears sufficient. Non-prior-art grounds should be fully developed rather than boilerplate. Some limited situations justify focusing on a particular issue: (A) application too informal for complete action (MPEP §702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims with no election (MPEP §2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder (MPEP §§803, 810, 812.01); (D) perpetual motion disclosures—cite best prior art. If res judicata, new matter, inoperativeness, etc., accompany with other available grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments contain inaccuracies, the examiner should notify as set forth in MPEP §714, subsection II.G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See referenced MPEP subsection for procedures and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in each Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: In every Office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number and its treatment or status given; include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PTO-326 'Office Action Summary'. Treat multiple dependent claims by treating each version separately (see MPEP §608.01(n) and Nested Bean v. Big Beings IPR2020-01234). Keep the Index of Claims up to date per MPEP §719.04. Claims retain their original numerals through prosecution for traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: State when claims are allowable; assist pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is apparent, examiners should draft one or more claims for pro se applicants and indicate such claims would be allowed if incorporated, and otherwise indicate allowable subject matter and suggest definite corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expedites prosecution for pro se inventors. If claims are allowable except for form defects or omission of a limitation, offer constructive suggestions and consider suggesting an interview. Use form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, 7.43.02, and 7.97. If a claim is allowable but dependent on a canceled or rejected claim, state it would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering paragraphs in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the Office action consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbering facilitates identification in future prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on examples, tests, and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned by the examiner unless there is a reasonable basis for questioning the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner questions results, appropriate claims may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for insufficient disclosure (see In re Borkowski). Applicant must reply with actual test results or arguments showing reason to believe predicted results; avoid entering new matter. If operability or utility is in question, consider a 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection. See MPEP §§2161–2164.08(c) for written description and enablement discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and initialing; contact information in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action and the name/telephone of the examiner to be contacted for interviews or discussion must appear in the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 to provide contact details. Include full surname and telephone number for the examiner to be called. Provide supervisor contact if examiner unreachable. Encourage use of USPTO Automated Interview Request (AIR) Form. Include duty hours, schedule details, and follow bracket instructions in the form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing, entry, dating, mailing, and returned Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions must be signed by an authorized signatory examiner, soft-scanned into the IFW, and mailed; the mailing date should be stamped or printed after action is written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistant examiner may initial; authorized examiner must sign promptly. The action is soft scanned into the image file wrapper and copies are mailed or given electronically. If Office action is returned undelivered, technical support staff should check address, re-mail with 'remailed' stamp if needed, notify applicant with letter and copy, add envelope and letter to electronic file, and consider restart of reply period when appropriate (see MPEP §710.06). Failure to receive reply after remailing may result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination and list of special cases (advancement under 37 CFR 1.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications are assigned to Technology Centers and are ordinarily examined in filing order, except for applications advanced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.102 or other Director orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is generally given to applications with the oldest claimed domestic benefit date. The order of examination gives priority to reissue applications (esp. in litigation), reexamination proceedings in litigation, inter partes reexamination in litigation, and special cases with fixed due dates. A list of grounds for petitions to make an application special includes applicant's age/health, inventions enhancing environment, energy, or countering terrorism (no fee), and prioritized examination requests (must meet filing/fee/claim limits). Prioritized examination restrictions: no more than four independent claims, no more than thirty total claims, no multiple dependent claims, not accorded to certain application types (design, reissue, provisional, reexamination, certain PCT national stage), and a cap of 15,000 requests per fiscal year. See 37 CFR 1.102 and MPEP for detailed filing and fee requirements and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and actions that take precedence; prompt action when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain procedures take precedence over other actions (e.g., printer rush allowed cases, reissue applications in litigation), and examiners should act forthwith if an application is in condition for allowance or needs final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: complete papers typed and ready for signature should be completed and mailed; allowed cases marked 'Printer Rush' processed promptly; reissue applications in litigation prioritized; actions with set periods (e.g., examiner's answers) take priority over special cases without fixed dates. If an examiner is satisfied the application is in condition for allowance or needs final rejection, they should act without awaiting the application's turn.
